run_64ms.result: every functional step passed, light and dark; the log check failed on script budget overruns
run_64ms.summary: After the go, the shell journey ran at the runtime's 64 ms script budget. The first attempt stopped at a test bug, the new rail check also counting the tab title and 'Saved' (fixed in ui.py; the app was right). The next two attempts passed every functional step of the shell journey, light and dark: Read mode (enter, turn a page, zoom, exit on the same page and zoom), find from the top bar alone with the left panel given back, a highlight and its reply, Pages, Combine, Fill & Sign, Edit with Alignment and Colour, save, and the damaged file (41 frames, through d10-damaged). Each then failed only the log check (check_log), on script budget overruns, and so restart, full and empty did not run.
overruns: the second attempt (23:56 to 23:59 on 10 Oct, California time): two 'script time budget exceeded' (its log's lines 1200 and 1215) around a 555 ms UI-thread stall in pdf.save, reported at line 1214: a file rename (octosense_engine_area::Stage::commit), then the removal of its staging folder. The third attempt overwrote that log; run-64ms/attempt-2-excerpt.txt holds the lines read from it before then

the third attempt (00:14 to 00:17 on 11 Oct): one, logged after a 262 ms UI-thread stall in the render cache's file rename (pdf.page, cache::store, Area::write), with only image decoding in between; its logs are kept, sanitized, in run-64ms/
run_64ms.cause: App Hub dispatches a host service inline from host.request, on the UI thread (#399), so a slow file rename counts against the calling script's 64 ms wall-clock budget. Those service paths (pdf.save's commit, the render cache's write) are unchanged by this pull request.
run_64ms.load: the one-minute load average was 54.8 to 56.9 just after the second attempt and 74.1 just after the third: six cargo builds and tests of other sessions at once, the malware scanner at 130 to 200% CPU, and the media analysis daemon at 150%. The evidence runs at --budget-ms 1000 ended at 10.7. Earlier on 10 Oct, at load 15 to 35, this folder's first round (before Read mode, one search and the review's fixes) passed all four runs at 64 ms with no overrun; its receipt is in this branch's history.
run_64ms.decision: the four evidence runs that follow used --budget-ms 1000, as #473's fixture run once did
run_64ms.log: run-64ms/shell.log and run-64ms/ui.log: the third attempt's shell and driver logs, with machine-local paths replaced by placeholders; run-64ms/attempt-2-excerpt.txt: the second attempt's error and hang lines, read from its log before the third attempt overwrote it
